rows.description: A teenager finds a photo or clip shared with cruel comments and feels exposed and helpless. Saving evidence, telling a trusted adult, reporting and blocking are practical steps, and it is never the target's fault.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult scrolls through friends' holidays, weddings and job news and feels behind. Posts show highlights only; limiting time and remembering this helps mood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult forwards a shocking message in a family group without checking it, believing it is important. Rumours travel fast and can harm; pausing, checking the source and skipping the forward are responsible acts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A user watches thousands attack a person over a clip and feels the pull to join. Seeing that most such stories are partial, and refusing to add cruelty, is a quiet act of fairness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional curates a public image for jobs and followers and feels the strain of performing. Some curation is normal; staying honest and keeping private spaces protects the self.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult chooses times without a phone, mutes accounts that drain them and keeps real friendships in real life. Small boundaries protect attention and calm without cutting off useful connection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
rows.description: A toddler visiting relatives abroad is held by strangers in some places and kept apart in others, and reacts to touch differently. Physical closeness norms vary widely and children read adult comfort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
rows.description: A child taught that looking an elder in the eye is rude meets a teacher who says look at me when I speak. The same behaviour carries opposite meanings, and children need patient translation between the two.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
rows.description: A teenager on an exchange notices that people abroad say no bluntly while at home a no is softened with maybe. Neither is rude in its own setting; learning to read both is a skill.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Global cultures: eye contact, personal space, directness and time
rows.description: A young adult standing close to a colleague abroad sees them step back, feels rejected and only later learns of different comfort distances. Noticing others' body language and adjusting is basic courtesy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
